profile.reading:
DataBank IAD1 sits at 21635 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, Virginia, one of three DataBank buildings in Ashburn known collectively as the Ashburn campus (IAD1, IAD3, IAD4). DataBank's own Northern Virginia and Ashburn campus overview pages give IAD1 85,330 square feet of IT space, 9.9 megawatts of critical IT load, and 18 onsite network carriers, but unlike IAD3 and IAD4, DataBank does not currently maintain a standalone spec-sheet page for IAD1 specifically; its figures come only from the aggregated campus and regional overview pages. A third-party aggregator states IAD1 was originally built in 2009, developed by Latisys, acquired by Zayo's zColo business in February 2015, and acquired by DataBank in December 2020, with a PUE of 1.5 and N+1 UPS design; DataBank's own site does not repeat any of this ownership history, so it is noted here as third-party-sourced and unconfirmed rather than adopted as fact. Across the full Ashburn campus, DataBank states 355,330 square feet of IT space and 69.9 megawatts of critical IT load on 18 acres, backed by roughly 70 megawatts of utility substation power; DataBank's Ashburn pages do not name the power utility, though Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley" as a matter of general public record. Loudoun County's own economic development materials describe the county as home to more than 9 million square feet of data center space and claim a majority of world internet traffic passes through networks based there, underscoring Ashburn's position as the largest concentration of interconnection-dependent data center capacity in the world, of which DataBank's Ashburn campus is one of many operators present.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley has driven repeated Dominion Energy transmission and generation investment cited in the utility's integrated resource plans and periodic rate cases before the Virginia State Corporation Commission, as regional data center demand, including DataBank's three-building Ashburn campus, has become the single largest driver of the utility's near-term capital spending in its Virginia service territory. Loudoun County's data center tax base has become a significant share of the county's overall commercial property tax revenue, a dynamic local officials have weighed against community concerns over land use, noise, and grid capacity as the sector has expanded well beyond its original fiber-optic-hub origins in the 1990s and early 2000s.

sources.title: Loudoun County Department of Economic Development, Data Centers

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own Northern Virginia market page gave a full address, IT capacity, and sqft for a previously address-less row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own Northern Virginia market overview page, fetched this session, describes this facility as IAD1, on the Ashburn Campus, and gives its address as 21635 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, VA 20147, with 9.9 MW of critical IT load and 85,330 IT square feet.

reading.body:
Databank Ashburn IAD1 is a 9.9 MW facility on Red Rum Drive in Ashburn, Virginia. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this IT load translates to roughly 250 racks, which is a modest footprint for current large-scale AI infrastructure. The facility occupies 85,330 square feet of technical space, yielding approximately 3 watts per square foot of published IT load.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish capacity figures, totaling 1,375 MW. Databank Ashburn IAD1 ranks 24th among the 23 published facilities in the state, meaning it falls just outside the top tier. The facility does not establish any binding constraint on AI compute scaling; it serves the published capacity baseline that other Virginia sites exceed.

No certifications, network carriers, cooling approach, or power source are published for this facility. No tenant names appear in the operator's specifications.
